subject: Packaging & price alignment — proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Sam Timmons <sam.timmons@fluxdata.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Packaging & price alignment — RFP follow-up

Irene —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We promised our procurement team we'd get competing quotes collected and a short summary so they can decide whether to pursue a full migration. Attached is the CloudCore pricing and the internal RFP requirements that drove their quote.

High level asks from FluxData procurement:
- Can Redwood match CloudCore's effective unit price for our inference usage profile (see page 2 of attachment)?
- If price-match is possible, what packaging/concessions do you require (commit term, seat counts, pilot credits, migration credits)?
- What does a 60–90 day migration path look like (who owns data egress, onboard resources, cutover support)?

We have a compliance checklist that will come later, but for commercial evaluation procurement wants to understand economics and gating items first. Can you send a comparably structured offer and a short migration checklist?

Attachment: flux_rfp_cloudcore_quote.pdf (PDF, 85KB)

Best,
Sam Timmons
Head of AI Ops
FluxData
procurement@fluxdata.io
415-555-0132
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging & price alignment — RFP follow-up

Sam —

Appreciate the context and the CloudCore quote; that helps a lot. I can absolutely put together a structured offer that mirrors the CloudCore economics and maps to your migration timeline, with a couple of tradeoffs to protect both sides. Quick summary up front (details attached):

What we can do now
- Price-match: we can match the competitor’s effective unit price for the first 12 months subject to a 12-month committed term and a minimum monthly usage threshold (details in the attachment).
- Migration support: 100 hours of engineering migration support + 2 weeks prioritized onboarding during cutover.
- Pilot credits: $40k in pilot credits applied pro rata over the first 60 days for validation/benchmarks.

What we’ll ask for in return
- 12-month commitment with a four-week lead time to schedule dedicated capacity for your peak windows.
- Standard Redwood terms (limited commercial carveouts). If you need a broad indemnity or data residency change we’ll have to review with legal and that may change pricing.

Next steps
- I’ve attached a short proposal (redwood_proposal_v1.pdf) and a pricing comparison worksheet. Can we do a 30-minute call tomorrow or Monday to lock the commit and timeline? Proposed times: Mon 5/3 10:00am PT or Mon 5/3 3:00pm PT.

Attachments: redwood_proposal_v1.pdf (PDF, 95KB)

If that sounds reasonable I’ll pull Jordan and Marissa into the contract conversation so we can move quickly.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T10:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Packaging & price alignment — asks from FluxData

Team — forwarding FluxData’s ask. Key facts:
- Deal: FLX-2027-0087
- External anchor: CloudCore effective price (see their quote).
- They want a direct price-match + migration path.

My recommended posture:
1) Offer an exact first-year effective price match if they sign a 12-month commitment at the same usage profile and accept Redwood's baseline terms. No one-off indemnity expansion.
2) Pilot credits: $40k as I proposed.
3) Migration credits: cover engineering time (100 hrs) + 2 weeks dedicated SRE support; do NOT cover egress costs beyond a capped amount (we'll propose $10k egress credit).
4) Require a brief operational checklist signed at SOW: Helm/infra access, test dataset snapshot, and weekly sync for 6 weeks post-cutover.

Risks:
- If procurement pushes for unlimited T&Cs changes we'll need to push back; pricing only holds if terms are baseline.
- If they want a shorter commit (6 months) economics get worse; consider offering a smaller pilot credit and shorter dedicated support window instead.

Ask: Jordan — can you prepare a 1-pager commercial term sheet and channel how aggressive we want to be on the $40k pilot vs. guaranteed term? Marissa — can you confirm ops can cover 100 hrs + 2 weeks SRE for May/June? Karthik — flag any commercial/legal clauses we should pre-clear.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the 1-pager and we’ll push a revised offer.

-- Irene
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Timmons <sam.timmons@fluxdata.io>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Revised offer: price-match structure and migration checklist

Sam —

Thanks for the call this morning. Per our conversation, attached are the items we discussed: a line-item price comparison, the formalized commercial offer, and a short migration checklist. High level summary below so procurement can review quickly.

Commercial offer (summary)
- Effective price-match for months 0–12 if Flux signs a 12-month committed term with a minimum monthly usage of 4M tokens (template in the attached pricing_comparison_v3.xlsx).
- Pilot & migration credits: $40k pilot credit + $10k capped egress credit (applied during the first 90 days).
- Engineering support: 100 dedicated migration hours + 2-week prioritized SRE window at cutover.
- Billing: monthly invoices, net 30.
- Legal: baseline Redwood terms attached (redwood_terms_snippet.pdf). Any redlines beyond routine securables (SLA tweaks, minor data residency notes) will require legal review and could adjust pricing.

Operational checklist (short)
- Provide sample inference traffic profile and representative model weights (non-PII).
- Temporary cross-account access to staging VPC for performance tests (IAM policy stub attached).
- Two-week validation window, weekly checkpoint calls.

DocuSign & timeline
- If Flux confirms by 5/7 we can schedule migration resources for a mid-May pilot and a late-May main cutover. I’ve also created a DocuSign packet to speed signatures: https://www.docusign.com/FLX-2027-0087

Attachments: pricing_comparison_v3.xlsx (Excel, 62KB); redwood_terms_snippet.pdf (PDF, 18KB)

Let me know if procurement needs the commercial sheet as a CSV or a different breakdown. If the legal team has specific redlines please send them to jordan_blake@redwood.com so we can triage.

Best,
Irene
From: Sam Timmons <sam.timmons@fluxdata.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Next steps:
- I’ll get DocuSign approved internally and return a signed packet by 5/6 if possible.
- Legal will reach out with redlines (likely limited).

Thanks for moving quickly on this. I’ll put procurement on standby for the DocuSign link.

— Sam
